lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.title: Mastery check: matching task size to time

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 1: Home Care Routines That Last
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice matching task size to time. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: With a trusted adult's permission, the learner selects two real tasks around the household that differ noticeably in size, such as wiping down one counter versus sorting a full shelf of items.
safetyNotes: A trusted adult approves both chosen tasks in advance and confirms neither one involves anything sharp, hot, high up, or otherwise unsafe for the learner to do alone.
If either task turns out to involve something unexpected and unsafe once started, the learner stops and checks with the adult before continuing.
The learner uses only a timer or clock during this task and only cleaning materials the adult has already approved for the learner's independent use.

simulationAlternative.description: If two real tasks of different sizes aren't available right now, the learner instead reads two written task descriptions of different sizes, one small and one larger, writes a time estimate for each based on what the description involves, and explains what specific details in each description led to a shorter or longer estimate.

materials: adult-or-local: two real household tasks of noticeably different sizes, approved by a trusted adult
learner-local: paper or a notes app

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Explain what you will do differently next time you estimate how long a task will take, based on which of your two estimates today was more accurate and why.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Estimation reasoning: Each estimate is based on a stated reason connected to the task's size or number of steps. | Accuracy analysis: The learner accurately reports the actual time for each task and correctly identifies which estimate was further off. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner estimate and time a third real task of a size between the first two and check whether their estimating accuracy improved compared to the first two tasks.

resources.title: matching task size to time worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: With a trusted adult's permission, the learner selects two real tasks around the household that differ noticeably in size, such as wiping down one counter versus sorting a full shelf of items.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact matching task size to time decision or action.
Model move 2: With your adult, pick two real tasks that are clearly different sizes.
Model move 3: Before starting either task, write down how many minutes you think each one will take and why.

Model check: Estimation reasoning: Each estimate is based on a stated reason connected to the task's size or number of steps. | Accuracy analysis: The learner accurately reports the actual time for each task and correctly identifies which estimate was further off.

resources.title: matching task size to time action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal for matching task size to time.
2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-model-card.
3. Do one coached move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-guided-card.
4. Complete the chosen route on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-independent-card.
5. Save the small record on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-evidence-record; use swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-retry-pair if a step is missed.

resources.title: matching task size to time coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: With a trusted adult's permission, the learner selects two real tasks around the household that differ noticeably in size, such as wiping down one counter versus sorting a full shelf of items.
Coach direction: With your adult, pick two real tasks that are clearly different sizes.
Learner prompt: Name your two tasks and explain what makes one clearly smaller or bigger than the other.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: matching task size to time complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Before starting either task, write down how many minutes you think each one will take and why.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I wrote a specific time estimate in minutes for each task before starting either one.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I gave a reason for each estimate based on the size or steps of the task, not a guess.
Response 3 (t2-p3): My adult reviewed and approved both tasks before I started the timer.

Equal-access rule: If two real tasks of different sizes aren't available right now, the learner instead reads two written task descriptions of different sizes, one small and one larger, writes a time estimate for each based on what the description involves, and explains what specific details in each description led to a shorter or longer estimate.

resources.title: matching task size to time minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain what you will do differently next time you estimate how long a task will take, based on which of your two estimates today was more accurate and why.

Success checks: Estimation reasoning: Each estimate is based on a stated reason connected to the task's size or number of steps. | Accuracy analysis: The learner accurately reports the actual time for each task and correctly identifies which estimate was further off.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: matching task size to time supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional matching task size to time condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Estimation reasoning: Each estimate is based on a stated reason connected to the task's size or number of steps. | Accuracy analysis: The learner accurately reports the actual time for each task and correctly identifies which estimate was further off..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l05-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

realRoute.title: matching task size to time — permitted real-life route

steps: Confirm the setting, materials, and stop condition before acting.

guardianInvolvement.role: Give permission; provide only the supervision, handling, review, or observation named in the lesson; attest only that the physical event occurred.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.
doNotCollect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations
account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details
photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
